Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.

- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.

- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.

- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.

items.says: Remove your date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are not relevant to product hiring and can create avoidable bias or compliance concerns.

items.says: Fix the late-delivery metric.
items.because: It changes the measurement method, not the actual operational performance, and may be seen as manipulating the metric.

items.says: Remove or correct the 'new merchant' bullet under the hospital consulting practicum.
items.because: It is nearly identical to the Harbor Payments onboarding bullet and refers to merchants in a hospital context, creating a major credibility problem.

items.says: Clarify the scope and causality of the Harbor Payments metrics.
items.because: The bullet does not specify the time period, sample size, test design, or whether the result was measured through an experiment.

items.says: Reconsider the phrase 'for all merchants' unless you can substantiate that scope.
items.because: It sounds unusually broad for a summer intern project.

items.says: Resolve the overlap between your two onboarding bullets.
items.because: The relationship between the onboarding redesign and the measurement bullet is not clear.

items.says: Clarify what you personally changed and how the pilot’s scope and results were measured.
items.because: The 9-to-4-day improvement and 2,300-merchant scope are compelling, but the narrative is unclear.

items.says: Explain why the opt-in comparison was appropriate and what limitations it had.
items.because: If this was observational rather than randomized, make that distinction clear.

items.says: Correct grammar and tense.
items.because: The S&OP bullet uses present tense ('prepares') while the role is in the past.

items.says: Clarify the currency for the 1.1 million-dollar estimate and whether it was annualized exposure, actual losses, or projected savings.
Make the connection between the research, business case, and roadmap decision more precise.
Clarify whether you personally resolved 140 tickets or coordinated their resolution.
State what kind of onboarding problems the tickets represented if there is room.
Clarify your analytical contribution to the slotting redesign and distinguish your work from the supervisors’ and pickers’ implementation work.
If the 30% reduction was sustained over a defined period, include that context.
Clarify whether you led implementation, requirements gathering, rollout, training, or adoption.
Explain whether the 1,800 annual hours are measured savings, estimated savings, or projected savings.
If the tool had an adoption or utilization rate, that could be more persuasive than training volume alone.
Clarify your role in the launch and distinguish app users from total student reach.
Clarify whether the 9 tonnes figure is measured or estimated.
Clarify whether the increase in weekly active users was directly attributed to the reminder feature or observed after launch.
Verify that the time period is clear: 'following term' is less precise than a defined measurement window.
Clarify whether you designed the volunteer shift system, implemented it, or coordinated volunteers manually.
Explain whether the reduction from 10 to 2 staff shifts was a direct result of the system.
Specify the product or operational problem addressed by the sessions and identify the output.
Quantify the improvement if you have it and clarify your contribution to mapping and redesign.
State how adoption was verified rather than simply saying the changes were adopted.
Separate methods from tools more clearly in the skills section.
If you list A/B testing, the resume should clearly show an experiment or controlled comparison.
items.because: Your experimentation evidence is not fully clear because one bullet describes opt-in comparisons rather than necessarily an A/B test.

items.says: Add a brief product-oriented summary or positioning line.
items.because: Your resume currently makes the reader infer that you are pursuing product management.

items.says: Standardize tense and spelling throughout the resume.
